name: Dental midline correction

lead: The dental midline is the line between the upper or lower central incisors. If the upper and lower midlines do not match, it is called a deviation.
Correction usually refers to orthodontic alignment, but the sources reviewed do not describe methods or outcomes.

paras: Orthodontic tooth movement shifts the arches so the midlines coincide. The sources reviewed give no details.
Not covered by the sources reviewed.

lead: Dental midline correction is the adjustment of teeth, usually through orthodontic treatment, so that the midline between the upper or lower central incisors lines up with the midline of the face or the opposing arch. The dental midline is defined as the midsagittal line of the upper and lower dental arches when the teeth are in maximum intercuspation and have ideal size, shape and position.[1]

Each arch has its own midline, marking the contact between the central incisors. When the lower teeth shift sideways relative to the upper, the midline is considered deviated; Wikipedia's example is a lower shift of about 2 mm.[1]

In looksmaxxing discussions, midline alignment is treated as one component of smile and facial symmetry. The sources reviewed contain no clinical studies or community material on correction methods or on how midline deviation affects perceived attractiveness.
infobox: Midsagittal line of the dental arches[1]

paras: The dental midline refers to the contact point between the mesial surfaces of the central incisors in each arch. A deviation exists when the midlines of the upper and lower arches do not coincide.[1] The source is a short reference entry and does not discuss relation to the facial midline, treatment, or how deviations are perceived.
